standard_prerequisites.name: Enumerable set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set is enumerable when it is empty or is the image of a surjection from the positive integers.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the starting point of the equivalence chain (source lines 973-974).

standard_prerequisites.name: Replacing a surjection by a bijection
standard_prerequisites.statement: A surjection from the positive integers onto A can be converted into a bijection onto A from the positive integers or from a finite initial segment (the author's proposition prop:enum-bij, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied in the middle of the chain (source lines 974-977).

standard_prerequisites.name: Shifting an enumeration between the positive integers and the naturals
standard_prerequisites.statement: An enumeration indexed by the positive integers can be reindexed by the natural numbers and conversely (the author's proposition prop:enum-shift, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the last step of the chain, changing the index set from the positive integers to the naturals or an initial segment starting at 0 (source lines 977-980).

core_obligations: Unfold enumerability: rewrite the left-hand side as emptiness or the existence of a surjection from the positive integers onto A (source lines 973-974).
Replace the surjection by a bijection: apply the retained proposition prop:enum-bij to pass to a bijection from the positive integers or from a finite initial segment (source lines 974-977).

Reindex to the natural numbers: apply the same argument as in the proof of the retained proposition prop:enum-shift to obtain a bijection from the natural numbers or from an initial segment of them, completing the equivalence (source lines 977-980).

proof_roadmap.step: Unfold enumerability as emptiness or a surjection from the positive integers.
Apply prop:enum-bij to convert the surjection into a bijection from the positive integers or an initial segment.
Apply the shift argument of prop:enum-shift to reindex by the natural numbers or an initial segment starting at 0.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own corollary cor:enum-nat-bij at source lines 966-970: a set A is enumerable if and only if A is empty or there is a bijection onto A from the natural numbers or from an initial segment of them. The proof at source lines 972-980 is a three-step equivalence chain and is not a restatement of the definition. It begins from the definition of enumerability as emptiness or the existence of a surjection from the positive integers, then applies the author's proposition that a surjection from the positive integers can be replaced by a bijection from the positive integers or a finite initial segment, and finally needs the index shift between the positive integers and the natural numbers, which is supplied by the author's separate proposition on shifting an enumeration and is applied by the same argument as in that proof. Keeping track of which domain (positive integers versus naturals, and whether the initial segment starts at 0 or 1) is allowed at each step is the substance of the proof, and the statement mentions none of it. The two invoked propositions are author results of the same unit and are retained as context so both references resolve inside the package.
